sample.label: sync-bifurcation-as-knob
sample.rationale: Both formalize the Kuramoto synchronization threshold as a designed musical control, not just a physics fact — one on a torus's two phasors, one on a population of spiking neurons. control-vocabulary-math's K_c ('below it the crowd drifts, above it synchrony switches on') is the same object as Three Kinds of Warp's type-3 lock/drift bifurcation ('a snap, not a fade'), same math, different material.
sample.evidence: control-vocabulary-math: 'The critical coupling K_c is the threshold where r lifts off zero — below it the crowd drifts, above it synchrony switches on.' Three Kinds of Warp: 'Below the synchronization threshold the rotation numbers shift... above threshold they lock... Bends the lattice itself... The Kuramoto coupling f1 = K sin(phi2-phi1) is the canonical instance.'

sample.label: worked-control-vocabulary
sample.rationale: Infeasible DSP Now Shippable names 'control-surface design is the hardest problem in the suite' and its own Forward Vectors say 'invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces — the concrete form of the hardest problem.' control-vocabulary-math is a worked instance of exactly that: it collapses a 16-64-neuron Kuramoto population into four performable knobs (K, sigma_threshold, frequency spread, drive) with r as the single closing-the-loop readout.
sample.evidence: Infeasible DSP Now Shippable: 'control-surface design is the hardest problem in the suite... Invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces — the concrete form of the hardest problem.' control-vocabulary-math: 'This document formalizes the layer that sits on top of that engine: the statistical descriptors that turn a noisy crowd of N spiking neurons into four or five smooth, performable knobs.'

sample.label: resists-dissolution
sample.rationale: Dissolutions' own Forward Vectors ask whether it needs a 'Refusals' sibling — 'entries that resist dissolution despite looking like they should merge.' Three Kinds of Warp's 1D obstruction theorem is exactly that structural refusal: no amount of clever type-1 phase reshaping (the move every commercial wavetable warp makes) can ever become type-2 or type-3 and produce inharmonicity — two things that look mergeable (more sophisticated warping = eventually inharmonic) and provably are not.
sample.evidence: Dissolutions: 'Does the catalogue eventually grow a sibling — Refusals, the entries that resist dissolution despite looking like they should merge? Two things that keep being mistaken for one and shouldn't be?' Three Kinds of Warp: 'The theorem holds for any warp at all... Every commercial wavetable warp redistributes energy among the harmonic slots; none of them moves a partial between slots... Structurally cannot produce inharmonicity.'
